name: Jasperware (Neoclassical)
summary: A fine, dense, unglazed stoneware that Josiah Wedgwood made from 1775. It is stained in pale blue, green or lilac and carries white relief figures in the classical manner.

philosophy.core_thesis: A matt coloured stoneware with white Greek and Roman reliefs lets an English factory make the antique world for the library table.
design_principles: Stain the whole body, not only the surface, with cobalt, so that the blue shows in each chip.
Leave the surface unglazed and fine-polished, so that it has a velvet matt look.
Press each white relief in a pitcher mould, 1 to 3 mm thick, and fix it to the damp body with water.
Take the figures from Greek vases and Roman gems: dancing women, sacrifices, Cupid and muses.
Use the solid jasper for fine pieces and the jasper dip, a thin coloured skin on a white body, for cheaper pieces.
Divide the surface into bands: a laurel or key-pattern border, a main frieze and a plain foot.
Fire the body once to full density at about 1200 to 1250 °C.
Mark the base with the factory name impressed in the clay.
anti_patterns: A glossy glaze over the relief
Reliefs that are thick and soft, with no sharp edge

form.shape: Urns, vases with a lid, ewers, pedestal vases and small bowls, after antique marble, bronze and Greek pottery.
form.profile: A clear classical outline: a round or egg-shaped body, a high foot with a square plinth, and a lid with an acorn or a knob.
form.foot_and_rim: A square or round plinth foot that is turned sharp; the rim is a plain band or a row of egg-and-dart.
form.proportion: Height 10 to 35 cm; the wall is 4 to 7 mm thick, and the plinth is one fifth of the height.
rules: Keep the outline simple, so that the reliefs are the ornament.
Turn the foot and the edges sharp on a lathe.
Place the relief frieze at the widest part of the body.

bodies.rule: Use a dense white stoneware of barium sulphate, clay, flint and flux, stained through with metal oxides. Black basalt is its dark companion body.

methods: throwing and turning on a lathe
sprig moulding of the white reliefs
forming.joins: Each relief is cut from the mould, wetted and pressed onto the body; fine undercut edges are trimmed with a knife.
forming.details: A sharp, undercut edge to each relief, a faint seam of the mould that the finisher removes, and an impressed mark on the base.

glaze.pattern: A frieze of white figures from antique art on a pale ground, with a laurel, a key pattern or a flower swag as border.
glaze.gloss: Matt to satin, about 2 to 10 GU; the surface looks like fine-grained stone.
glaze.wear: The surface takes grease and marks; a chipped relief shows the white clay, and a sharp edge softens with use.

palette.strategy: A matt single ground colour in a pale tone, with the white relief as the only contrast.

firing.kiln: A coal-fired bottle kiln, with the pieces in saggars.
processes: mixing of the stained body in the slip house
moulding and pressing of the white reliefs
fixing of the sprigs to the damp body
a single firing to full density
fine polishing of the foot on the lathe
firing.scale: A factory line of the 1780s and after: many sets of the same relief, with a skilled worker for each stage.
firing.signs: A matt, even ground; undercut relief edges; and a slight warp where the base rested on the saggar.

pieces.form: Pedestal urn with a lid and a frieze of dancing women on a blue ground
Egg-shaped vase with a laurel border and a Cupid frieze
Round lidded jar with an acorn knob and a key-pattern band
Footed bowl with a muses frieze outside, in green jasper
Black basalt vase with a plain foot and a narrow white band

positive: neoclassical urn on a library table

evidence.title: Jasperware vase with white reliefs, V&A
An Offering to Peace, jasper plaque, MET 3638

emotion.target_response: A feeling of order and learned calm: the viewer sees a cool pale ground and white figures, and thinks of a library, a museum and ancient Rome.

use_cases: a neoclassical urn or vase for a Georgian interior
a pale blue and white product brief
a museum label on English stoneware of 1780
avoid_when: the brief needs a high-gloss glaze
the brief needs rustic or hand-thrown irregular form

modifiers.how: Change to an earthenware body with lead glaze and slip trail; drop the sharp reliefs.
Swap the stained jasper for a plain pale glazed body and keep the classical outline.

wall_thickness.note: The wall is thick compared with porcelain, because jasper is a dense stoneware.
